title: Cherry baked oats with crispy bacon

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, eggs, milk, honey, vanilla, butter, cherries and bacon are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item, and 300g of British cherries in July is a normal seasonal buy.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a baking dish, roasting tray, bowl, whisk and knife, with simple mixing and baking.

works.reason: 200g oats to 400ml milk and 2 eggs, baked for 35 minutes at 190°C, is a sound baked-oats ratio for four, and streaky bacon crisps in 15 minutes on the shelf below.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers halving and stoning 300g of cherries and whisking the mix, and the 35-minute cook matches the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Cherries are the main fruit through and on top of the bake, which suits a July breakfast.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oats, eggs, fruit and bacon make a filling breakfast, with only modest added honey.
